verdict.summary: You can create a HubSpot OAuth app with the CLI and connect your own account in under an hour, with no review. Your own app is capped, though: 10 allowlisted accounts if private (100 for Solutions Partners), or 25 installs if set to marketplace distribution. Going past 25 requires an approved Marketplace listing, and to submit one you need 3 active installs from accounts outside your organisation plus a minimal set of scopes.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours to set up the app; 1-2 days to prepare listing pages and materials, plus the time it takes to get 3 outside installs
verdict.approval_wait: None for up to 25 installs. Marketplace listing review: first response within about 10 business days, per a third-party guide (not confirmed by HubSpot).

steps.title: Create a free HubSpot developer account
steps.detail: On developers.hubspot.com, choose 'Create developer account' and sign up.

steps.title: Install the HubSpot CLI and authenticate it
steps.detail: Install the HubSpot CLI, then log it in to your developer account. Apps on developer platform v2025.2 and v2026.03 can only be created through the CLI.
gotchas: Don't start a legacy public app or a 2023.2/2025.1 project. From Nov 2, 2026, Marketplace listings for those are rejected.

steps.title: Create the project and write app-hsmeta.json
steps.detail: Create a new app project with the CLI. In app-hsmeta.json, set distribution ('private' or 'marketplace'), set auth.type to 'oauth', add the Composio callback to auth.redirectUrls, and list your scopes in requiredScopes and optionalScopes.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

values.label: distribution
values.value: marketplace (up to 25 installs, no allowlist) or private (up to 10 allowlisted accounts)

gotchas: Composio's default scope list has 33 entries, including legacy scopes (content, e-commerce, accounting, timeline). Keep only the ones your agent calls. Listing and certification reviews reject scopes the app doesn't use.
Users can only install the app if they have access to every required scope, so put scopes you can live without in optionalScopes.

steps.title: Upload the project to your developer account
steps.detail: Run the CLI upload command so HubSpot creates the app from your *-hsmeta.json files.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and client secret
steps.detail: On the project details page, open the app and click the Auth tab. Under 'Client credentials', copy the Client ID and Client secret.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config with your own credentials
steps.detail: In Composio, create a HubSpot OAuth2 auth config that uses your own app. Paste in the client ID and secret, and enter the same scopes you put in app-hsmeta.json. Composio's managed app uses the authorize URL https://app.hubspot.com/oauth/authorize and the v1 token URL.
gotchas: HubSpot is deprecating the OAuth v1 token endpoint, and new Marketplace listings must use the endpoints with dates in the path (e.g. /oauth/2026-03/token). Check which token endpoint Composio uses for your config.

steps.title: Connect your own HubSpot account and test
steps.detail: Start a connection from Composio and approve the consent screen. Then make one API call and confirm the token refreshes after the 30-minute access-token lifetime. After the first tokens are issued, the app shows up under Connected Apps in that HubSpot account.
gotchas: A refresh that fails with invalid_grant / BAD_REFRESH_TOKEN means the refresh token was revoked or is invalid, and the user has to reconnect.
Don't cap the length of stored tokens. HubSpot doesn't define a maximum size.

steps.title: Let invited accounts install the app
steps.detail: For private distribution, add up to 10 customer accounts to the allowlist (100 if you're a Solutions Partner). For marketplace distribution, share the install link; up to 25 accounts can install before your listing is approved. Community reports say you need to accept the Acceptable Use Policy and that users will see an 'unverified' warning.
gotchas: HubSpot staff say they can't make exceptions to the install caps.

steps.title: Prepare listing pages and the scope justification
steps.detail: Draft a public privacy policy, terms of service, support URL and setup page. Make the listing's Shared data table match the scopes you request exactly, and remove any scope the app hasn't used in the last 30 days.

steps.title: Get 3 active installs from outside your organisation
steps.detail: Get at least 3 production HubSpot accounts that aren't affiliated with you to install the app and use it within the past 30 days.

steps.title: Submit the Marketplace listing
steps.detail: In your developer account, submit the app listing. Before submitting, confirm the app uses OAuth only, runs on v2025.2 or v2026.03, and uses the token, introspect and revoke endpoints with dates in the path. Testing credentials have not been required since March 31, 2026.

steps.title: Wait for HubSpot's listing review
steps.detail: A third-party guide reports a first review within about 10 business days, with up to 60 days to respond to HubSpot's feedback. Once the listing is approved, the 25-install cap is removed.

steps.title: (Optional) Apply for certification
steps.detail: Certification is separate from listing and not required. It needs 60+ active outside installs, a demo video, a verified domain, use of the uninstall API, and a security questionnaire on how you store and protect OAuth tokens.

requirements.detail: Needed to create and upload apps.
OAuth is required to install the app in more than one account, whether allowlisted or through the Marketplace.
Each needs activity in the past 30 days before you can list.

requirements.item: Minimal scopes matching the Shared data table
requirements.detail: Request only scopes the app uses; HubSpot checks this against your API logs.

requirements.item: Supported platform version and OAuth endpoints with dates in the path
requirements.detail: From Nov 2, 2026, new listings must be on v2025.2/v2026.03 and use the endpoints with dates in the path (e.g. /oauth/2026-03/token).

requirements.item: Privacy policy, terms, support URL, setup page
requirements.detail: Must be public. This comes from community and third-party sources.

scopes.effect: Core CRM scopes. Request only the objects your agent actually reads or writes; the listing review rejects scopes the app doesn't use.

scopes.scope: content, e-commerce, accounting, timeline (legacy scopes in Composio's default list)
scopes.effect: These are in Composio's broad default list. Remove them unless you use them, or they can block listing and certification.
A broad admin-level scope in Composio's default list. Users without access to a required scope can't install the app, so make it optional or drop it.
Requesting them triggers a security questionnaire on how you store and protect tokens. Apps with app cards can't request them.

blockers.symptom: Installs stop at 25 (marketplace distribution) or at 10/100 (private distribution)
blockers.cause: HubSpot caps installs for v2025.2+ apps until the Marketplace listing is approved.
blockers.fix: Get 3 active outside installs and get the Marketplace listing approved. HubSpot will not raise the cap otherwise.

blockers.symptom: UNLISTED_APP_OVER_PRIVATE_INSTALL_LIMIT when migrating a legacy app
blockers.cause: The legacy app already has more than 25 installs.
blockers.fix: List the app on the Marketplace before migrating, or start a new v2025.2/v2026.03 app.

blockers.symptom: Listing or certification rejected for extraneous scopes
blockers.cause: The app requests scopes it hasn't used in the last 30 days of API logs, or its screenshots don't match the current scopes.
blockers.fix: Trim requiredScopes to the scopes you actually call and update the Shared data table.

blockers.symptom: Listing rejected for platform version or OAuth endpoint
blockers.cause: From Nov 2, 2026, legacy apps, 2023.2/2025.1 projects and OAuth v1 endpoints are rejected for new listings.
blockers.fix: Build on v2025.2 or v2026.03 and use the endpoints with dates in the path (e.g. /oauth/2026-03/token).

blockers.symptom: A user can't install the app
blockers.cause: The user doesn't have access to all of the app's required scopes.
blockers.fix: Move scopes you can do without into optionalScopes.

composio.note: Composio's managed HubSpot app is the fastest way to prototype. Register your own app when you want your own branding on the consent screen, a smaller scope list (Composio's default is broad and includes legacy scopes), or control over install caps. Your own app is capped at 25 installs with marketplace distribution, or 10 allowlisted accounts with private distribution (100 for Solutions Partners), until HubSpot approves its Marketplace listing. Add Composio's callback URL to auth.redirectUrls in app-hsmeta.json. Composio's managed config uses the OAuth v1 token endpoint, which HubSpot is deprecating, and new listings must use the endpoints with dates in the path.

evidence.claim: Composio offers managed HubSpot OAuth2 with authorize URL https://app.hubspot.com/oauth/authorize, token URL https://api.hubapi.com/oauth/v1/token and 33 broad default scopes.
The developer portal is public and links to free developer account signup.
evidence.quote: Create developer account with a HubSpot Developer account

evidence.claim: The authorize endpoint is live and returns a JS 'HubSpot OAuth' page even for an invalid client_id.
Apps on v2025.2/v2026.03 are created with the HubSpot CLI, and their configuration lives in *-hsmeta.json files that you upload.
evidence.quote: Apps on the new developer platform (versions `2025.2` and `2026.03`) are initialized using the HubSpot CLI

evidence.claim: app-hsmeta.json declares distribution, auth.type oauth, redirectUrls and the scope lists.
evidence.quote: "auth": {       "type": "oauth",       "redirectUrls": ["http://localhost:3000/oauth-callback"],       "requiredScopes"

evidence.claim: The client ID and secret are on the app's Auth tab under Client credentials.
evidence.quote: Click the **Auth** tab. * Under *Client credentials*, copy the *Client ID* and *Client secret*

evidence.claim: OAuth is required to distribute an app to multiple accounts.
evidence.quote: If you plan on distributing your app to multiple accounts (either with a specific set of allowlisted accounts or via the HubSpot app marketplace), you'll need to set up OAuth

evidence.claim: Access tokens last 30 minutes, refresh tokens are long-term, and token size has no defined maximum.
evidence.quote: Access tokens are short-lived (30 minutes), and you can check the `expires_in` parameter when generating an access token to determine its lifetime (in seconds).

evidence.claim: The new OAuth endpoints return RFC 6749 errors such as invalid_grant for a bad refresh token.
evidence.quote: refresh token is invalid, expired or revoked

evidence.claim: Marketplace-distribution v2025.2 apps are capped at 25 installs until listed; private OAuth apps are capped at 10 accounts, or 100 for Solutions Partners.
evidence.quote: apps that are created or migrated to version 2025.2 are capped at 25 installs until they are listed on the HubSpot Marketplace

evidence.claim: An approved listing removes the 25-install cap, and you can switch from private to marketplace distribution without interrupting installs.
evidence.quote: which removes the 25‑install cap on marketplace distribution once your listing is approved

evidence.claim: HubSpot staff say they can't make exceptions to install limits; legacy apps over 25 installs hit UNLISTED_APP_OVER_PRIVATE_INSTALL_LIMIT when migrating.
evidence.quote: we aren’t able to make exceptions regarding the app install limits

evidence.claim: Community advice: use marketplace distribution and sign the AUP to skip the allowlist; the app shows as unverified until HubSpot reviews it.
evidence.quote: It will continue to say the app is unverified until you get it reviewed by hubspot

evidence.claim: Listing requires a single app ID, OAuth only, 3 active unaffiliated installs and minimal scopes reflected in the Shared data table.
evidence.quote: your app must have at least three active, unique installs.

evidence.claim: Apps with app cards must not request sensitive data scopes; sensitive scopes involve a security questionnaire.
evidence.quote: Your app must not access, request, or use sensitive data scopes.

evidence.claim: From Nov 2, 2026, new listings must be on v2025.2/v2026.03 and use the date-versioned OAuth endpoints because v1 is deprecated; testing credentials have not been required since March 31, 2026.
evidence.quote: OAuth v1 endpoints are being deprecated and will be replaced by the latest OAuth API endpoints

evidence.claim: Certification and sensitive-scope requests require a questionnaire on how OAuth tokens are accessed and stored.
evidence.quote: The questionnaire extends beyond certification and will also be implemented for other programs, such as requesting access to sensitive data scopes.

evidence.claim: Optional certification needs 60+ active installs, a demo video, a verified domain and use of the uninstall API.
evidence.quote: Your app must have at least 60 [active](#activity), unique installs

evidence.claim: Extraneous scopes, judged against the last 30 days of API logs, must be removed.
evidence.quote: Extraneous scopes must be removed.

evidence.claim: Third-party guide: first listing review within about 10 business days, with up to 60 days after feedback; needs a privacy policy, terms and support URL.
evidence.quote: an initial review within 10 business days, and up to 60 days from the time HubSpot shares feedback

evidence.claim: Community answer: listing needs a setup page, terms page, privacy policy page and 3 unique installs.
evidence.quote: 1. Setup page 2. t&c page 3. privacy policy page 4. 3 unique installs

evidence.claim: Only users with access to an app's required scopes can install it; the app appears under Connected Apps after the first tokens are issued.

open_questions: Does HubSpot OAuth support PKCE? Not confirmed.
How long do refresh tokens last? The docs only say 'long-term'.
Redirect URL rules are unconfirmed: whether HTTPS is required, whether localhost is allowed in production, and whether matching is exact.
Which scopes count as 'sensitive data scopes', and what is the full process for requesting them?
Does Composio's managed app still use the deprecated /oauth/v1/token endpoint, and when will v1 stop working?
The 'unverified app' consent warning and the Acceptable Use Policy step are reported only by community sources.
HubSpot hasn't published a listing review timeline. The 10-business-day figure comes from a third-party guide.
Are any of Composio's broad default scopes (e.g. settings.users.write, accounting, e-commerce) sensitive, and would they trigger extra review for your own app?
